literal: Cui Xian; Gao Dezheng; Cui Ang
idiomatic: Cui Xian; Gao Dezheng; Cui Ang

literal: Cui Xian, styled Jilun, was a man of Anping in Boling commandery, a descendant of Cui Shi, Han Minister of Works, and for generations a prominent clan of the northern provinces.
idiomatic: Cui Xian, styled Jilun, was a man of Anping in Boling commandery, a descendant of Cui Shi, Han minister of works, and for generations a leading house of the northern provinces.

literal: His father Mu was a commandery clerk.
idiomatic: His father Mu was a commandery clerk.

literal: In youth Xian was a student; he fled to Bohai and relied on Gao Gan, giving his sister in marriage to Gan's brother Shen.
idiomatic: In youth Xian was a student; he fled to Bohai and attached himself to Gao Gan, giving his sister in marriage to Gan's brother Shen.

literal: When Shen later held Guangzhou, he had Xian appointed chief clerk.
idiomatic: When Shen later governed Guangzhou, he had Xian appointed chief clerk.

literal: Duke of Zhao Commandery Chen, defending Dingzhou, engaged him as deliberator of the grand marshalate.
idiomatic: Duke of Zhao Commandery Chen, defending Dingzhou, engaged him as deliberator of the grand marshalate.

literal: Following Chen to Jinyang, Gao Huan conversed with him and was pleased, appointing him acting chief clerk to the chancellor.
idiomatic: Following Chen to Jinyang, Gao Huan conversed with him and was pleased, appointing him acting chief clerk to the chancellor.

literal: When Gao Huan raised troops to enter Luoyang, he left Xian to assist Chen in managing rear affairs.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised troops to enter Luoyang, he left Xian to assist Chen in managing affairs behind the lines.

literal: He said to him: "When men know one another, is it a matter of new or old?
idiomatic: He said to him, "When men know one another, is it a matter of new or old?

literal: Military affairs are weighty, and the duty of staying behind is pressing; my younger brother is young and not yet versed in affairs—for every matter behind, I entrust all to you.
idiomatic: Military affairs are weighty and the duty of holding the rear is pressing; my younger brother is young and not yet versed in affairs—for every matter behind, I entrust all to you.

literal: " They clasped hands earnestly, three or four times.
idiomatic: " They clasped hands earnestly, three or four times over.

literal: Later he was moved to left vice director and director of the ministry of personnel, and took chief part in deliberating the Linzhi Code.
idiomatic: Later he was moved to left vice director and director of the ministry of personnel, and took chief part in deliberating the Linzhi Code.

literal: Xian's personal favor grew day by day; he delighted in recommending men of talent.
idiomatic: Xian's personal favor grew day by day; he delighted in recommending men of talent.

literal: He said Xing Shao was fit for a staff post with access to secret affairs; Gao Cheng thereupon summoned Shao, who was greatly favored and trusted.
idiomatic: He said Xing Shao was fit for a staff post with access to secret affairs; Gao Cheng thereupon summoned Shao, who was greatly favored and trusted.

literal: In the course of talk, Shao then slandered Xian.
idiomatic: In the course of talk, Shao then slandered Xian.

literal: Gao Cheng was displeased and said to Xian: "You speak of Zicai's strengths, yet Zicai speaks only of your faults—this is a foolish man.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng was displeased and said to Xian, "You speak of Zicai's strengths, yet Zicai speaks only of your faults—this is a foolish man.

literal: " Xian said: "Zicai speaks of Xian's faults; Xian speaks of Zicai's strengths—each states what is true, without rancor.
idiomatic: " Xian said, "Zicai speaks of Xian's faults; Xian speaks of Zicai's strengths—each states what is true, without rancor.

literal: When Gao Shen rebelled, having a rift with Xian, Gao Huan wished to kill him; Gao Cheng rescued and pardoned him.
idiomatic: When Gao Shen rebelled, having a rift with Xian, Gao Huan wished to kill him; Gao Cheng rescued and pardoned him.

literal: At the beginning of Wuding, he was moved to chief inspector; he selected Bi Yiyun, Lu Qian, Song Qindao, Li Yin, Cui Zhan, Du Rui, Ji Ye, Li Bowei, Cui Ziwu, and Li Guang as inspectors—men of the age called this knowing men.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuding, he was moved to chief inspector; he selected Bi Yiyun, Lu Qian, Song Qindao, Li Yin, Cui Zhan, Du Rui, Ji Ye, Li Bowei, Cui Ziwu, and Li Guang as inspectors—men of the age called this knowing men.

literal: Gao Cheng wished to lend Xian imposing bearing; with the lords seated, he had Xian walk in with head high and slow steps, two men tugging his robes to lead him in; Gao Cheng faced him across the hall and bowed with equal ceremony.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng wished to lend Xian imposing bearing; with the lords seated, he had Xian walk in with head high and slow steps, two men tugging his robes to lead him in; Gao Cheng faced him across the hall and bowed with equal ceremony.

literal: Xian would not yield the seat but sat down; after two rounds of wine he took his leave.
idiomatic: Xian would not yield the seat but sat down; after two rounds of wine he took his leave.

literal: Gao Cheng said: "This humble officer has a modest vegetarian meal; I hope you will stay a little.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng said, "This humble officer has a modest vegetarian meal; I hope you will stay a little.

literal: " Xian said: "I have just received orders to inspect at the bureau.
idiomatic: " Xian said, "I have just received orders to inspect at the bureau.

literal: " Without waiting for the meal he left; Gao Cheng descended the steps to see him off.
idiomatic: " Without waiting for the meal he left; Gao Cheng descended the steps to see him off.

literal: Ten days later, Gao Cheng went out to the eastern hills with the lords and met Xian on the road; the outriders were struck with red staffs and Gao Cheng turned his horse aside to avoid him.
idiomatic: Ten days later, Gao Cheng went out to the eastern hills with the lords and met Xian on the road; the outriders were struck with red staffs and Gao Cheng turned his horse aside to avoid him.

literal: Xian successively memorialized and impeached Minister of Works Sima Ziru and the minister Yuan Xian and Administrator of Yong province Murong Xian, also impeached Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang Wang Tan and Inspector of Bing province Kezhuhun Daoyuan—the charges written to the utmost; all were removed from office.
idiomatic: Xian successively memorialized and impeached Minister of Works Sima Ziru, the minister Yuan Xian, and Administrator of Yong province Murong Xian, and also impeached Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang Wang Tan and inspector of Bing province Kezhuhun Daoyuan—the charges written to the utmost; all were removed from office.

literal: Of the rest, those killed or dismissed were very many.
idiomatic: Of the rest, those killed or dismissed were very many.

literal: Gao Huan wrote to the nobles at Ye: "Cui Xian once served my younger brother as chief clerk of Dingzhou, later my son's grand marshalate deliberator, and when moved to left vice director and director of the ministry of personnel I did not yet know his ability.
idiomatic: Gao Huan wrote to the nobles at Ye, "Cui Xian once served my younger brother as chief clerk of Dingzhou, later my son's grand marshalate deliberator, and when moved to left vice director and director of the ministry of personnel I did not yet know his ability.

literal: Only when he took the inspectorate did he correct and impeach thus.
idiomatic: Only when he took the inspectorate did he correct and impeach thus.

literal: Prince of Xianyang and Minister Sima were both my old companions of common cloth opposite the gate, honored and intimate beyond all others; at the same time they incurred guilt—I could not save them; gentlemen, be wary.
idiomatic: Prince of Xianyang and Minister Sima were both my old companions of common cloth opposite the gate, honored and intimate beyond all others; at the same time they incurred guilt—I could not save them; gentlemen, be wary.

literal: " When Gao Huan went to the capital, the officials welcomed him at Zimo.
idiomatic: " When Gao Huan went to the capital, the officials welcomed him at Zimo.

literal: Gao Huan took Xian's hand and praised him: "Before, was there no judge in the court? Yet greed ran through the realm and none would impeach.
idiomatic: Gao Huan took Xian's hand and praised him, "Before, was there no judge in the court? Yet greed ran through the realm and none would impeach.

literal: The chief inspector has devoted his heart to the state, not avoiding the powerful, and thus near and far are brought to order and the lords uphold the law.
idiomatic: The chief inspector has devoted his heart to the state, not avoiding the powerful, and thus near and far are brought to order and the lords uphold the law.

literal: To charge battle lines—there are many such men; to hold office with upright countenance—only now do I see it.
idiomatic: To charge battle lines—there are many such men; to hold office with upright countenance—only now do I see it.

literal: Wealth and glory today are simply what the chief inspector has earned for himself; father and son Gao Huan have no way to repay it.
idiomatic: Wealth and glory today are simply what the chief inspector has earned for himself; father and son Gao Huan have no way to repay it.

literal: " He granted Xian a fine horse and had him ride alongside, talking as they went.
idiomatic: " He granted Xian a fine horse and had him ride alongside, talking as they went.

literal: Xian bowed; the horse bolted in fright; Gao Huan embraced him and handed him the reins.
idiomatic: Xian bowed; the horse bolted in fright; Gao Huan embraced him and handed him the reins.

literal: The Wei emperor feasted at Hualin Garden and said to Gao Huan: "Of late, court nobles, prefects and county chiefs, and the hundred offices in every place have many been greedy and violent, encroaching on inferiors.
idiomatic: The Wei emperor feasted at Hualin Garden and said to Gao Huan, "Of late, court nobles, prefects and county chiefs, and the hundred offices in every place have many been greedy and violent, encroaching on inferiors.

literal: In the court there are those who apply their hearts with fairness and impeach in straight speech, not avoiding kin—Wang may urge them to drink.
idiomatic: In the court there are those who apply their hearts with fairness and impeach in straight speech, not avoiding kin—Wang may urge them to drink.

literal: " Gao Huan descended the steps, knelt, and said: "Only Chief Inspector Cui Xian, one man.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan descended the steps, knelt, and said, "Only Chief Inspector Cui Xian, one man.

literal: Reverently following the clear command, I dare urge wine upon him—and furthermore the thousand bolts of cloth from my archery gift, I beg they be turned and given to him.
idiomatic: Reverently following the clear command, I dare urge wine upon him—and furthermore the thousand bolts of cloth from my archery gift, I beg they be turned and given to him.

literal: " The emperor said: "Chief Inspector Cui upholds the law; ways and customs are alike regulated.
idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Chief Inspector Cui upholds the law; ways and customs are alike regulated.

literal: " Xian thanked him: "This is from Your Majesty's transforming influence, and the urging and reward of my lord the Grand General Cheng.
idiomatic: " Xian thanked him, "This is from Your Majesty's transforming influence, and the urging and reward of my lord Grand General Cheng.

literal: " Gao Cheng withdrew and said to Xian: "I still fear those impeachments—how much more others.
idiomatic: " Gao Cheng withdrew and said to Xian, "I still fear those impeachments—how much more others.

literal: " Thereafter his awe-inspiring name grew daily; inside and outside none did not fear and submit.
idiomatic: " Thereafter his awe-inspiring name grew daily; inside and outside none did not fear and submit.

literal: When Gao Huan died, before the mourning was announced, Gao Cheng made Xian director of the revenue section and concurrent vice director, entrusting him with matters close to the heart.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan died, before the mourning was announced, Gao Cheng made Xian director of the revenue section and concurrent vice director, entrusting him with matters close to the heart.

literal: Xian worried for the state as for his home, taking the realm as his charge.
idiomatic: Xian worried for the state as for his home, taking the realm as his charge.

literal: Gao Cheng's carriages and dress exceeded measure, executions were irregular, and in speech and conduct there were sometimes faults; Xian each time spoke sternly and to the utmost, and Gao Cheng also stopped on his account.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng's carriages and dress exceeded measure, executions were irregular, and in speech and conduct there were sometimes faults; Xian each time spoke sternly and to the utmost, and Gao Cheng also stopped on his account.

literal: Several hundred prisoners—Gao Cheng wished to execute them all and daily pressed for the documents.
idiomatic: Several hundred prisoners—Gao Cheng wished to execute them all and daily pressed for the documents.

literal: Xian deliberately delayed them and did not submit in time; Gao Cheng's intent relaxed and in the end they were spared.
idiomatic: Xian deliberately delayed them and did not submit in time; Gao Cheng's intent relaxed and in the end they were spared.

literal: From his first entry into office he normally returned only at day's end.
idiomatic: From his first entry into office he normally returned only at day's end.

literal: At dawn he and his brothers would ask after their mother's health; at evening he would taste food and look in on her sleep, then go to the outer study to face kin and guests.
idiomatic: At dawn he and his brothers would ask after their mother's health; at evening he would taste food and look in on her sleep, then go to the outer study to face kin and guests.

literal: In a lifetime he did not inquire into household affairs.
idiomatic: In a lifetime he did not inquire into household affairs.

literal: When Wei and Liang made peace, the great and favored all sent men with the envoys to trade; Xian only asked that Buddhist sutras be sent.
idiomatic: When Wei and Liang made peace, the great and favored all sent men with the envoys to trade; Xian only asked that Buddhist sutras be sent.

literal: Emperor Wu of Liang heard of it, had them copied, and sent them to the lodge with streamers, flowers, precious canopies, hymns, and chants.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang heard of it, had them copied, and sent them to the lodge with streamers, flowers, precious canopies, hymns, and chants.

literal: Yet he loved grand talk and joking without restraint.
idiomatic: Yet he loved grand talk and joking without restraint.

literal: He secretly had the monk Mingzang compose the Treatise on Buddha-nature and affix his own name, transmitting it throughout the Jiang region.
idiomatic: He secretly had the monk Mingzang compose the Treatise on Buddha-nature and affix his own name, transmitting it throughout the Jiang region.

literal: His son Dana was thirteen; Xian had a Confucian named Quan Hui teach him to speak two words on the Book of Changes, then gathered court nobles and famous men and had Dana ascend the high seat to open a lecture.
idiomatic: His son Dana was thirteen; Xian had a Confucian named Quan Hui teach him to speak two words on the Book of Changes, then gathered court nobles and famous men and had Dana ascend the high seat to open a lecture.

literal: Mu Zhongrang of Zhao commandery was made to yield on the spot; Xian was pleased and promoted him to gentleman of the secretariat.
idiomatic: Mu Zhongrang of Zhao commandery was made to yield on the spot; Xian was pleased and promoted him to gentleman of the secretariat.

literal: Ye had a saying: "Two lines of lecture win a gentleman of the secretariat.
idiomatic: Ye had a saying, "Two lines of lecture win a gentleman of the secretariat.

literal: " These were all Xian's failings.
idiomatic: " These were all Xian's failings.

literal: When Gao Yang first succeeded to the hegemony, Sima Ziru and others, nursing old grudges, said Xian's crimes were heavy and that he ought to be punished.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang first succeeded to the hegemony, Sima Ziru and others, nursing old grudges, said Xian's crimes were heavy and that he ought to be punished.

literal: Gao Longzhi also said the government net should be widened, harsh inspecting judges removed, and Cui Xian dismissed—then near and far would be satisfied.
idiomatic: Gao Longzhi also said the government net should be widened, harsh inspecting judges removed, and Cui Xian dismissed—then near and far would be satisfied.

literal: Gao Yang followed this.
idiomatic: Gao Yang followed this.

literal: When he took the throne, those who slandered him still did not cease.
idiomatic: When he took the throne, those who slandered him still did not cease.

literal: The emperor then had Commander Chen Shanti and others search Xian's house—it was very poor; only a thousand-odd pages of letters from Gao Huan and Gao Cheng to Xian, mostly discussing great military affairs.
idiomatic: Gao Yang then had Commander Chen Shanti and others search Xian's house—it was very poor; only a thousand-odd pages of letters from Gao Huan and Gao Cheng to Xian, mostly discussing great military affairs.

literal: The emperor sighed in admiration.
idiomatic: Gao Yang sighed in admiration.

literal: Still he could not silence everyone's mouths; he exiled Xian to Macheng—by day he carried earth for corvée, by night he was shut in a dungeon.
idiomatic: Still he could not silence everyone's mouths; he exiled Xian to Macheng—by day he carried earth for corvée, by night he was shut in a dungeon.

literal: After more than a year, a slave reported Xian plotted rebellion; he was chained and taken to Jinyang—without substance; he was released and comforted.
idiomatic: After more than a year, a slave reported Xian plotted rebellion; he was chained and taken to Jinyang—without substance; he was released and comforted.

literal: Soon he was moved to grand minister of ceremonial.
idiomatic: Soon he was moved to grand minister of ceremonial.

literal: The emperor said to the assembled ministers: "Grand Minister of Ceremonial Cui is pure and upright, without peer under heaven—you do not equal him.
idiomatic: Gao Yang said to the assembled ministers, "Grand Minister of Ceremonial Cui is pure and upright, without peer under heaven—you do not equal him.

literal: " Earlier, Gao Cheng had wished to marry his sister to Xian's son, but when Gao Cheng died the matter was dropped.
idiomatic: " Earlier, Gao Cheng had wished to marry his sister to Xian's son, but when Gao Cheng died the matter was dropped.

literal: At this time the ministers feasted in Xuanguang Hall; many sons of noble kin were there.
idiomatic: At this time the ministers feasted in Xuanguang Hall; many sons of noble kin were there.

literal: Gao Yang went round speaking with them; at the seat he personally wrote to Xian: "Your worthy son Dana is very talented in learning.
idiomatic: Gao Yang went round speaking with them; at the seat he personally wrote to Xian, "Your worthy son Dana is very talented in learning.

literal: My late elder brother's daughter, Princess Le'an, the Wei emperor's niece, honored inside and outside, surpasses my sisters—I think to fulfill my elder brother's longstanding wish.
idiomatic: My late elder brother's daughter, Princess Le'an, the Wei emperor's niece, honored inside and outside, surpasses my sisters—I think to fulfill my elder brother's longstanding wish.

literal: " He then gave the princess to Dana in marriage.
idiomatic: " He then gave the princess to Dana in marriage.

literal: At the end of Tianbao he was right vice director.
idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao he was right vice director.

literal: The emperor said to those about him: "Cui Xian admonishes me for drinking too much—but what harm is my drinking?
idiomatic: Gao Yang said to those about him, "Cui Xian admonishes me for drinking too much—but what harm is my drinking?

literal: " Prince of Changshan said privately to Xian: "The Supreme One may often be drunk; the empress dowager cannot yet speak up; we brothers hold our tongues—only you, vice director, dare to offend his countenance; inside and outside we are deeply moved and ashamed.
idiomatic: " Prince of Changshan said privately to Xian, "The Supreme One may often be drunk; the empress dowager cannot yet speak up; we brothers hold our tongues—only you, vice director, dare to offend his countenance; inside and outside we are deeply moved and ashamed.

literal: " In the tenth year Xian died of illness; the emperor stroked the bier and wept.
idiomatic: " In the tenth year Xian died of illness; Gao Yang stroked the bier and wept.

literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as grand marshalate.
idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as grand marshalate.

literal: Dana was gentle, good, pure, and careful, with knowledge and learning; in youth he held office as minister of the state granaries.
idiomatic: Dana was gentle, good, pure, and careful, with knowledge and learning; in youth he held office as minister of the state granaries.

literal: After entering Zhou he plotted rebellion and was executed.
idiomatic: After entering Zhou he plotted rebellion and was executed.

literal: In the Tianbao era Gao Yang once asked Princess Le'an: "How does Dana compare with you?
idiomatic: In the Tianbao era Gao Yang once asked Princess Le'an, "How does Dana compare with you?

literal: " She answered: "We greatly respect each other—only Mother-in-law hates the boy.
idiomatic: " She answered, "We greatly respect each other—only Mother-in-law hates the boy.

literal: " Gao Yang summoned Dana's mother into the palace, killed her, and threw the body into the Zhang River.
idiomatic: " Gao Yang summoned Dana's mother into the palace, killed her, and threw the body into the Zhang River.

literal: When Qi was destroyed, Dana killed the princess to avenge his mother.
idiomatic: When Qi was destroyed, Dana killed the princess to avenge his mother.

literal: Gao Dezheng, styled Shizhen, was a man of Su in Bohai.
idiomatic: Gao Dezheng, styled Shizhen, was a man of Su in Bohai.

literal: His father Hao was Wei inspector of Cangzhou.
idiomatic: His father Hao was Wei inspector of Cangzhou.

literal: Dezheng was clever and keen in youth, with spirit and dignified bearing.
idiomatic: Dezheng was clever and keen in youth, with spirit and dignified bearing.

literal: Gao Yang brought him in as staff officer to the grand marshalate in charge of records, and was very intimate.
idiomatic: Gao Yang brought him in as staff officer to the grand marshalate in charge of records, and was very intimate.

literal: Gao Huan also promoted him as staff officer to the chancellor's residence, entrusting him as confidant.
idiomatic: Gao Huan also promoted him as staff officer to the chancellor's residence, entrusting him as confidant.

literal: He was moved to gentleman of the yellow gates.
idiomatic: He was moved to gentleman of the yellow gates.

literal: Gao Cheng succeeded to the enterprise; he went to Jinyang; Gao Yang remained in the capital as defender; he had Dezheng share in secret affairs, and favor grew still greater.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng succeeded to the enterprise and went to Jinyang; Gao Yang remained in the capital as defender and had Dezheng share in secret affairs, and favor grew still greater.

literal: Gao Cheng died suddenly; affairs came in haste and the mood of the masses was disorderly.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng died suddenly; affairs came in haste and the mood of the masses was disorderly.

literal: The meritorious generals held that continuing the military enterprise was weighty and urged the emperor to go quickly to Jinyang.
idiomatic: The meritorious generals held that continuing the military enterprise was weighty and urged Gao Yang to go quickly to Jinyang.

literal: The emperor also hesitated and could not decide; in the night he summoned Yang Yin, Du Bi, Cui Jishu, and Dezheng and others, and only then settled the plan.
idiomatic: Gao Yang also hesitated and could not decide; in the night he summoned Yang Yin, Du Bi, Cui Jishu, Dezheng, and others, and only then settled the plan.

literal: Yang Yin was left to hold the capital.
idiomatic: Yang Yin was left to hold the capital.

literal: Dezheng and the emperor had long been intimate and affectionate; in speech nothing was withheld.
idiomatic: Dezheng and Gao Yang had long been intimate and affectionate; in speech nothing was withheld.

literal: Regular attendant Xu Zhicai and retainer Song Jingye were versed first in astronomy and apocrypha; also Chen Shanti's household retainer Yang Zishu had connections—all through Dezheng urged Gao Yang to carry out the abdication and succession.
idiomatic: Regular attendant Xu Zhicai and retainer Song Jingye were versed first in astronomy and apocrypha; also Chen Shanti's household retainer Yang Zishu had connections—all through Dezheng urged Gao Yang to carry out the abdication and succession.
